messages.author: a532c7cff19936e8
messages.subject: ranef and pcountopen
parts:
Hi,

Does ranef for the pcountopen function use the improper prior f(N_{it}) \propto 1 leading to

E(N_{it})=n_{it}/\hat{p}+(1-\hat{p})/\hat{p}?  (The same as was used in Dali and Madsen (2011) that resulted in equation (11) on page 581.)

If yes then is \hat{p} computed using the predict function with syntax predict(fit,newdata=covs,type="det")?

Thanks for your help,

Russ

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] ranef and pcountopen
parts:
Hi Russell,

ranef does not use the improper prior, and I'm not sure why they suggested such a prior in their paper. ranef uses the priors specified by the arguments "mixture" and "dynamics".

You can compute estimates of p using predict.

Best,
Richard

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] ranef and pcountopen
parts:
Hi Russ,

There is no closed form of the posterior, but you can compute it using the forward or backward algorithms that are commonly used in the analysis of hidden Markov models. I implemented the backward algorithm following the approached outlined in one of the appendices of the original paper. Note that this involves summing over all possible value of N (up to K) for each site/primary-period, which takes a ton of time. MCMC can actually be faster when N is high.

Confidence intervals can be computed as quantiles of the posterior, which is demonstrated on the ranef help page. Source code is here: 

https://github.com/rbchan/unmarked/blob/master/R/ranef.R 

As is common in Empirical Bayes methods, the posterior distributions do not account for uncertainty about the hyperparameters (lambda, omega, gamma, etc...). I think you would have to adopt some sort of bootstrap to deal with that.

Richard
